newsitem.title: CHINA: China southern city plans long bridge to Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: China southern city plans long bridge to Hong Kong.

text.p: China's southern city of Zhuhai is applying for central government permission to build a 27-km (17-mile) road bridge to Hong Kong after the British colony returns to Chinese rule this year, the Xinhua news agency said.

Zhuhai city officials said preparatory work had already begun on the six-lane 13.4 billion yuan ($1.6 billion) bridge, which would have separate spans connecting islands in the seas between Hong Kong and the booming Chinese city.
Investment for the bridge would be raised by a Sino-foreign corporation, with construction to begin in 1998 and to be completed by 2004, Xinhua said in an overnight report.
"The bridge will be built to create a closer connection between western Guangdong province and Hong Kong and Macau," an official of the city's foreign affairs office said by telephone.

It would be the second road route from the mainland to Hong Kong, which returns to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30, after more than 150 years of British colonial rule. All land traffic to the British colony currently passes through the Lo Wu border point in Shenzhen, the official said.
"(The bridge) will ease the pressure of passenger and cargo flows on Lo Wu after Hong Kong's return," he said.
Investment in the 31-metre wide (100-ft) bridge was expected to be recovered within 18 years, Xinhua said but gave no further details.
The local official said the bridge was also designed to improve communications between Hong Kong and the Portuguese enclave of Macau, which neighbours Zhuhai and returns to Chinese rule in 1999.
Most travellers currently cross the Pearl River delta between Hong Kong and Macau by ferry, jetfoil or hovercraft.
